title: POC minimal retention patterns & legal Q&A
content:
Purpose:
Quick reference notes from the Nov 2025 SE/Legal workshop on minimal retention patterns for customer POCs. Goal: propose small, implementable patterns engineers can offer customers during early trials that minimize legal friction while keeping telemetry useful for debugging and performance tuning.

Context & assumptions:
- This doc is focused on POCs where customers want to test Redwood inference with sample private data but do not yet have an enterprise contract/DPA signed.
- POC durations typically 1–8 weeks.
- Customers vary: startups (low legal overhead) to regulated customers (health, finance) who require stricter controls.
- We assume hosted Redwood API by default unless customer requests Dedicated or Private.

High-level retention patterns (3 patterns to offer):
1) Ephemeral-session-only (strongly-recommended default for trials)
   - Request/response and KV cache kept only in-memory on inference nodes.
   - No persistent write to disk or long-term logs. KV cache TTL = session end.
   - Minimal request logs aggregated for SLO metrics (latency, error rate) but scrubbed: PII removed, only hashes retained if needed for dedup.
   - Use case: demos, sensitive demos, initial product evaluation.
   - Pros: minimal legal exposure; easy to explain to customers.
   - Cons: limited post-mortem capabilities for debugging complex SLO regressions.

2) Short-window POC store (7–30 days)
   - Requests and responses optionally persisted for a configurable short window (default: 14 days) then automatically deleted via retention job.
   - Data at rest encrypted (KMS) with customer-tenant separation for Dedicated/private POCs.
   - Logs are partitioned; access controls limit visibility to named SEs and the customer admin.
   - Pseudonymization step: first-class names/emails replaced with deterministic hash + salt per-customer to allow dedup without revealing raw PII. Salt rotation guidance included.
   - Use case: POCs requiring debugging across sessions, simple quality evaluation.

3) Pseudonymized long-term analytics (30+ days, opt-in)
   - Only aggregate analytics and pseudonymized dialogs retained beyond 30 days.
   - Original raw text purged; only tokenized/obfuscated records kept.
   - Explicit customer consent required and recorded in ticket/DPA addendum.
   - Use case: longitudinal model quality experiments, latency/cost trend analysis.

Specific controls (implementation notes):
- Input redaction pipeline: regex rules + model-based PII detector stage before persistence. Detector output stored as tags ("contains-email", "contains-ssn") rather than raw extraction.
- KV cache management: allow customer-configurable TTL; recommend max 24h for hosted POCs.
- Telemetry retention: traces/metrics retained as metrics-only (no raw prompts) for 90 days; traces that include prompt snapshots must follow the selected POC pattern.
- Audit trail: all retention changes require a ticket (Jira) and an audit log entry with owner and reason.

DPA addendum language snippets (for quick legal review; not final):
- "For the duration of the Pilot, Provider will retain Customer Input and Output only per the selected retention profile: Ephemeral-session-only, Short-window (14 days by default), or Pseudonymized long-term (opt-in)."
- "Provider will pseudonymize defined PII fields prior to any persistence; pseudonymization will be reversible only with Customer-held salt unless otherwise agreed."
- "Logs required for debugging will be accessible only to named SEs and will be deleted within X days per the retention profile."
- "Provider will not use Customer Input or Output to improve Provider models or training data unless Customer provides explicit written consent."

Privacy risk matrix (high level):
- Raw PII in persisted prompts: High risk -> Mitigation: default to ephemeral, apply PII detector and pseudonymization if persistence needed.
- Model leakage via embeddings or cache keys: Medium risk -> Mitigation: salt and namespace embeddings; prevent embedding export in hosted trials.
- Access control misconfiguration: High risk -> Mitigation: role-limited access, emergency access review, periodic audits.

Sample customer-facing checklist (what to ask on POC kickoff):
- POC duration and expected data sensitivity (low/medium/high).
- Preferred retention profile (Ephemeral / Short-window / Opt-in analytics).
- Required SE support level and which SEs are approved to view persisted data.
- Any legal/regulatory constraints (HIPAA, PCI, GLBA, etc.).
- Whether customer will provide salt/keys for pseudonymization or request provider-managed keys.

Notes from legal Q&A in the workshop (actionable items flagged):
- Legal: strongly prefers explicit line in addendum that "no use for model training" for trials. Action: add to template and flag to sales. Owner: Priya Kapoor.
- Engineering: needs a low-friction toggle in the console to flip retention profile per POC. Action: Console ticket. Owner: Liam Chen (see jira:SE-4821).
- SEs requested a standardized redaction/PII-detector config file for reuse across POCs. Action: create repo snippet + example config. Owner: Diego Martinez (github:repo/pocexamples).

Open questions (needs legal/ops input):
- Can we safely offer "reversible pseudonymization" with provider-held salt for startups that cannot manage keys? Legal wants preference for customer-held salt. (Decision needed.)
- If a customer opts into 30+ day pseudonymized analytics, do we need a separate opt-in ticket for model improvement usage, or will the single consent cover both analytics and training?
- For hosted POCs, is embedding export blocking feasible at platform level without a performance/regression risk? Engineering to prototype.

Implementation checklist for next sprint (Rough MVP for SEs to offer this month):
1) Console: retention-profile toggle + description copy (owner: Liam). Jira: SE-4821.
2) Back-end: ephemeral-only code path + retention enforcement job (owner: Diego).
3) Redaction/PII-detector: baseline regex + model detector + sample config (owner: Diego).
4) Legal: add DPA addendum boilerplate + review (owner: Priya).
5) SE kit: one-pager + kickoff checklist + email templates (owner: Maya).
